data.targetWord: The title meaning 'Awakened One' or 'Enlightened One', given to Siddhartha Gautama after his enlightenment

examples.en-GB: The Buddha taught the Four Noble Truths for 45 years after his enlightenment.

data.targetWord: The four encounters — old age, sickness, death, and a wandering holy man — that prompted Siddhartha to leave his palace and seek the truth about suffering

examples.en-GB: The Four Sights shattered Siddhartha's sheltered worldview and set him on the path to enlightenment.

data.targetWord: The path between extreme self-indulgence and extreme self-denial, discovered by the Buddha before his enlightenment

examples.en-GB: The Buddha rejected both palace luxury and harsh asceticism, choosing the Middle Way instead.

data.targetWord: The Buddha's foundational teaching: suffering exists (dukkha); it has a cause (craving); it can cease; the Eightfold Path leads out of it

examples.en-GB: The Four Noble Truths are like a medical diagnosis — identifying the problem, cause, cure, and treatment.

data.targetWord: The Pali word for suffering, dissatisfaction, or unsatisfactoriness; the first of the Four Noble Truths and one of the Three Marks of Existence

examples.en-GB: Dukkha includes not only physical pain but the impermanence of all pleasant things.

data.targetWord: The Buddha's practical guide to liberation, with eight steps divided into wisdom, ethical conduct, and mental training

examples.en-GB: The Eightfold Path includes Right Speech, Right Action, and Right Mindfulness.

data.targetWord: The Pali word for impermanence; the teaching that nothing lasts forever and all conditioned things change

examples.en-GB: Anicca means that even pleasant experiences are impermanent and will eventually end.

data.targetWord: The Buddhist teaching that there is no fixed, permanent self or soul; the self is a changing process, not a fixed entity

examples.en-GB: Anatta distinguishes Buddhist teaching from Hindu belief in the permanent atman (soul).

data.targetWord: Liberation from suffering and the cycle of rebirth; the ending of craving; the ultimate Buddhist goal

examples.en-GB: Nirvana is not a paradise like heaven — it is the extinguishing of craving and suffering.

data.targetWord: The cycle of birth, death, and rebirth, driven by craving and karma, from which Buddhists seek liberation

examples.en-GB: Following the Eightfold Path leads to liberation from samsara.

data.targetWord: The moral law of cause and effect; intentional actions have consequences that shape future lives and experiences

examples.en-GB: Acting with kindness creates positive karma; acting with cruelty creates negative karma.

data.targetWord: Five ethical guidelines voluntarily undertaken by Buddhists: no killing, no stealing, no sexual misconduct, no false speech, no intoxicants

examples.en-GB: The Five Precepts guide Buddhist behaviour in daily life at home, school, and work.

data.targetWord: The community of Buddhist practitioners; the third of the Three Jewels alongside the Buddha and Dharma

examples.en-GB: Taking refuge in the Sangha means committing to practise alongside other Buddhists.

data.targetWord: The three foundations of Buddhist life: the Buddha (teacher), the Dharma (teachings), and the Sangha (community)

examples.en-GB: Every Buddhist takes refuge in the Three Jewels as the basis of their practice.

data.targetWord: The Buddha's teachings and the cosmic truth they reveal; the second of the Three Jewels

examples.en-GB: Studying and practising the Dharma is central to the Buddhist path.

data.targetWord: The practice of training the mind through focused attention or insight, central to the Buddhist path

examples.en-GB: Buddhist meditation includes breath awareness (samatha) and insight practice (vipassana).

data.targetWord: Full, aware presence in each moment; noticing thoughts and experiences without clinging or being swept away

examples.en-GB: Right Mindfulness is one of the eight steps of the Eightfold Path.

data.targetWord: Loving-kindness; the wish for all beings to be happy; a key Buddhist virtue cultivated through meditation

examples.en-GB: Metta Bhavana meditation develops loving-kindness towards all beings, including strangers.

data.targetWord: Compassion; the wish for all beings to be free from suffering; a core Buddhist virtue

examples.en-GB: Karuna motivates Bodhisattvas to help others reach liberation before entering nirvana themselves.

data.targetWord: In Mahayana Buddhism, someone who has achieved enlightenment but chooses to remain in the cycle of rebirth to help all beings reach liberation

examples.en-GB: The Bodhisattva ideal emphasises compassion — delaying personal nirvana to help others.

data.targetWord: The most important Buddhist festival, celebrating the birth, enlightenment, and death of the Buddha on the same full moon day

examples.en-GB: Vesak is marked with temple visits, offerings, meditation, and acts of charity.

data.targetWord: The 'Way of the Elders' — the oldest surviving Buddhist tradition, practised mainly in Sri Lanka, Thailand, and Myanmar, emphasising the Pali Canon and monastic life

examples.en-GB: Theravada Buddhism emphasises individual effort and the monk or nun as the ideal practitioner.

data.targetWord: The 'Great Vehicle' — a major Buddhist tradition practised in China, Japan, and Korea, emphasising the Bodhisattva ideal and helping all beings reach liberation

examples.en-GB: Mahayana Buddhism includes the ideal of the Bodhisattva, who delays nirvana to help others.

data.targetWord: The profound awakening that the Buddha achieved — a full understanding of the nature of reality, suffering, and liberation

examples.en-GB: The Buddha achieved enlightenment after 49 days of meditation under the Bodhi tree.

data.targetWord: The Buddhist teaching that a continuum of consciousness passes through many lives; distinct from Hindu reincarnation as there is no permanent soul

examples.en-GB: Buddhist rebirth is like a flame passed from candle to candle — continuity without an unchanged entity.

data.title: Put these key events in the Buddha's life in the correct order
items: Siddhartha is born into a royal family and raised in luxury
Siddhartha encounters the Four Sights and decides to leave the palace
Siddhartha achieves enlightenment under the Bodhi tree
The Buddha teaches the Four Noble Truths at the Deer Park in Sarnath

data.title: Arrange the Four Noble Truths in the correct order
items: Samudaya — suffering is caused by craving and attachment
Nirodha — suffering can cease if craving is let go
Magga — the Noble Eightfold Path is the way out of suffering

data.title: Put the steps in a basic Buddhist breathing meditation in the correct order
items: Find a quiet, comfortable sitting position
Bring attention to the breath — noticing each inhale and exhale
When the mind wanders, gently return attention to the breath
Extend awareness and notice thoughts without following them
